Nationally, 35 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance while 59 percent disapprove as of August 19, leaving him significantly underwater with a net approval rating of -24, according to Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. The survey has garnered 124,759 responses since January 20, 2025, when Trump was inaugurated for a second term. [...] According to the Civiqs poll, Trump has the highest net approval rating in Wyoming, where 56 percent of voters approve of his performance and 35 disapprove—giving him a net approval rating of +22 when rounding up.

His net approval rating is also positive in several other states that make up the Republican heartland:

results.content: President Donald Trump's net approval rating has slipped into negative territory in eleven states Trump carried by at least ten points in 2024 — a shift that pushes his political challenges well past the handful of battlegrounds where erosion was already expected. A rolling online survey from Civiqs, built from more than 120,000 responses collected from registered voters since Trump's return to office in January 2025, puts him at 36 percent approval against 59 percent disapproval nationwide as [...] Civiqs is a scientific online polling firm directed by political scientist Drew Linzer and owned by Kos Media. results.title: Trump's Approval Turns Negative in 11 Red States He Won by Double Digits According to Civiqs Online Poll

results.content: Drew Linzer, the director of Civiqs, previously told the USA TODAY Network the firm uses advanced and proprietary modeling to develop results from online surveys of around 200 to 250 registered voters daily across the country. Voters in Colorado and other states are represented in the sample "proportional to the sizes of those states in the US population." Those results are part of the process used in calculating Trump’s approval rating in each state. [...] Civiqs, which offers regular updates from its online surveys, pegged approval in Colorado of Trump’s job performance at 31%, with disapproval at 64% on July 30 (4% said they neither approved nor disapproved).
